definition: a scene of complete disorder or chaos
hook: Shambles used to be a place you could actually visit, and it smelled terrible.
modernAnchor: A messy kitchen. A failed meeting. A plan that fell apart. We call it a shambles.
journey: Old English sceamol meant a stool or bench, the low table a seller set out his goods on.
Medieval towns gave the word to the meat market, the street where butchers laid out and cut their wares.
Those streets ran with blood and offal, so shambles came to mean a slaughterhouse, and then any scene of carnage.
By the 1900s the blood had drained away and only the mess remained. Any disaster could be a shambles.
